definitions.explanation: Having a pure, unspoiled quality free from malice or cunning. Describes someone, typically a child, who acts naturally without hidden motives. Generally positive or endearing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{無邪気|むじゃき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んでいる→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
{無邪気|むじゃき}な⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{癒|いや}された→癒す：13616_iyasu⟧。
examples.english: I was comforted by the innocent smile.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大人|おとな}→大人：02856_otona⟧になって⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{無邪気|むじゃき}な⟦ところ→所：01137_tokoro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あって→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{好|す}かれている→好く：30762_suku⟧。
examples.english: Even as an adult, she has an innocent quality that makes people around her fond of her.

notes:
USAGE:
Usually positive, describing a charming lack of guile. Most often said about children, but can describe adults with a childlike openness. Occasionally used with a slightly critical nuance when someone is obliviously naive in a situation that calls for caution.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無邪気|むじゃき}な⟦{笑顔|えがお}→笑顔：01884_egao⟧ (an innocent smile)
- {無邪気|むじゃき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{笑|わら}う→笑う：00685_warau⟧ (to laugh innocently)
- {無邪気|むじゃき}な⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧ども (an innocent child)
- {無邪気|むじゃき}な⟦{質問|しつもん}→質問：00888_shitsumon⟧ (an innocent question)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{純真|じゅんしん}→純真：18238_junshin⟧: pure; innocent — emphasizes moral purity and sincerity, slightly more literary
- ⟦{天真爛漫|てんしんらんまん}→天真爛漫：22150_tenshinranman⟧: naive and carefree — stronger emphasis on being uninhibited and spontaneous
